Caspr runs on a Research Budget — one monthly number that funds every analysis you run. No stacked subscription tiers, no token metering, no line-item invoice to decode.

You set a Research Budget, and each analysis draws from it at a fixed price: Brief $15, Study $80, Intelligence $300 in-budget ($399 à la carte), plus an optional Premium Data Add-on ($20–$60) shown and confirmed before the analysis starts. Whatever you don't spend carries forward automatically — you're billed for what you use, not for a budget you didn't touch.

The size of your Research Budget determines what you can access:

- Professional — $200/month, roughly $186 available for analyses. Brief and Study.
- Business — $600/month, roughly $558 available. Adds Intelligence, data upload, output editing, and follow-up refinement.
- Enterprise — $1,800/month, roughly $1,674 available, pooled across a team of three seats. Adds SSO and API access.

You're charged once a month. No separate bills for individual reports, no per-seat add-ons layered on top.

Before committing to a monthly number, start with the $100 Research Budget every new account receives free — no card required — and see exactly what $15 and $80 buy. See budgets.

A Research Budget is the single number you authorise each month — a pool of spend you draw analyses from, not a licence per seat or a fixed subscription tier.

Think of it as a research retainer you control directly, the way you'd control a budget line for external research, except you decide exactly how it gets spent, analysis by analysis. Every Brief, Study, or Intelligence analysis carries a fixed price, shown before you commit. Running one simply draws from the balance — no separate access fee to track, no token metering, no seat-by-seat billing to reconcile.

Unused balance carries forward automatically. Set a $200 budget and spend only $80 in a month, and the remaining balance isn't lost — it sits in your Wallet, ready for next month's analyses, on top of whatever the next recharge adds.

The budget amount also determines which features unlock — Business and Enterprise sit at higher thresholds — but that's a separate question from how much of it you spend in a given month.

New accounts start with a $100 gifted Research Budget, no credit card required, so you can run real analyses before committing to anything.

Start with $100 free.

Four prices, no fine print.

- Brief — $15. A focused 3–5 page briefing, ready in about 15 minutes.
- Study — $80. The full analysis: methodology, scenario work, a boardroom-ready PDF or editable PPTX.
- Intelligence — $300 drawn from your Research Budget, or $399 as a one-off with no subscription required. The deepest depth, built for board-level and diligence-grade decisions.
- Premium Data Add-on — $20–$60, only when an analysis calls for a source like Bloomberg or specialist regulatory data. You see the exact price and approve it before it's added.

The $200,000 question a strategy engagement would spend weeks answering costs $80 here, delivered in minutes, not months.

Every price is fixed and shown upfront — no metered tokens, no per-page charges, no surprise invoice after the report lands. Run one from $15.

Nothing happens to it — unused Research Budget carries forward automatically. You don't lose what you didn't spend.

Each month, Caspr recharges only the amount you actually used the month before — a delta recharge, not a flat renewal. Say you set a $200 budget: run one Study ($80) in a given month, and your next recharge restores only that $80. The rest of your balance, untouched, carries straight through to the new cycle rather than resetting to zero and forcing you to start over.

This is the default behaviour, not a setting to configure or a perk to request. There's no "use it or lose it" clock on your working balance, and no monthly allowance that expires unused. Your balance simply reflects real usage, cycle over cycle, for as long as the account stays active.

The only balances that do expire are gifted ones — your free trial's Research Budget, which has a 90-day window, and any promotional credits, which carry their own shorter terms. Balance you've paid for stays yours until you spend it.

See how budget works.

Three milestones — Professional, Business, and Enterprise — determine what's unlocked as your Research Budget grows. All three run the same core loop: prompt, layout, gate, boardroom-ready report. What changes across them is analysis depth, editing power, and team scale.

**Professional — $200/month budget, roughly $186 available for analyses.** The entry point for solo use. Run Brief and Study depth analyses — from a 3–5 page briefing note to a full weighing engagement with scenario analysis. You also get a standing Monthly Brief on a topic of your choosing and one Caspr Signals topic for weekly developments. Built for an individual analyst, researcher, or founder who needs analyst-grade output without a team or a retainer around it.

**Business — $600/month budget, roughly $558 available for analyses.** Everything in Professional, plus what turns Caspr from a one-shot report generator into a working research tool: **Intelligence** depth for the highest-rigour, multi-model analysis; **data upload** so your own files feed the analysis alongside Caspr's 25M+ sources; and **output editing**, including section refinement and follow-up queries, so a delivered report keeps evolving. Consulting teams, category managers, and corporate development functions running real due diligence tend to land here.

**Enterprise — $1,800/month budget, roughly $1,674 available, pooled across the team.** Everything in Business, plus **SSO**, **API access**, and **3 pooled seats** as standard — budget and every unlock shared across the team rather than licensed person by person, with an admin able to set per-user spending sub-limits. Built for organisations running Caspr as standing infrastructure: investment teams, agencies serving multiple clients, or strategy functions with several analysts drawing on one shared budget.

Each milestone is a budget threshold, not a separate product to sign up for — cross it, and the features unlock immediately. Start where your current usage sits; moving up is a budget change, not a new contract.

Choose your budget.

Yes. Intelligence — Caspr's deepest depth, built for due diligence and board-level strategy — is available at $399 per report with no Research Budget required. Add a card, run the analysis, done.

Both versions are the identical Intelligence engagement: the same source depth, the same rigour, the same citations. The only difference is how you pay for it. Buy an Intelligence report.

Every new account starts with a $100 Research Budget, gifted, no card required. It's yours to spend for 90 days.

$100 covers real testing, not a token demo: six Briefs at $15 each, or a full Study at $80 with room for a Brief besides. Run the depth that matches the question you actually have — a quick fact-check or the board-grade version — and see the report before you decide whether to set a monthly Research Budget of your own.

The 90-day window is the only constraint. Whatever balance remains when it lapses is forfeited, so the sooner you run your first analysis, the more of the $100 you put to work. There's no card on file forcing the decision — the clock is the only thing moving.

Most people don't need convincing after the first report. They need to see one. Claim $100 free.

Unused Research Budget is refunded in full if you cancel — Caspr doesn't hold onto money for analyses you never ran. Completed analyses aren't refunded, since the report was already delivered; the one exception is a system error that fails to produce output, in which case the full cost is credited back to your balance automatically, no request needed.

The $100 free trial balance is gifted, not paid, so it isn't refundable — spend it before the 90-day window closes.

If you believe an analysis produced materially incorrect output, contact support — each case is reviewed individually.

Changing your Research Budget is a single setting inside Wallet, not a budget swap or a new signup — adjust the monthly amount, confirm, done.

**Increasing your budget** unlocks the new milestone's features immediately on confirmation. Move from $200 to $600 and Intelligence, data upload, and output editing are available the moment you confirm — you don't wait for a billing cycle to use them. The higher budget amount itself, and the larger recharge that comes with it, takes effect at your next billing cycle; your current balance and cycle are unaffected until then.

**Decreasing your budget** works in reverse: the lower amount takes effect at your next billing cycle, and access to features above the new threshold is removed at the end of your current cycle, not the moment you confirm. Any analysis already running when a downgrade lands completes uninterrupted — nothing gets cut off mid-report.

There's a floor: you can't set a budget below $200, or below what your current balance requires. Caspr tells you the minimum if you try to go lower.

Billing stays simple throughout: one charge per month, and it only recharges what you actually spent the cycle before — never billed twice for the same period.

Upgrade your budget.

A strategy engagement with a firm like McKinsey or BCG starts above $50,000 and can run into the hundreds of thousands — with a multi-week timeline attached. Caspr delivers comparable depth from $15, in under 15 minutes.

Run the math on a Study: $80 against a $50,000 minimum engagement isn't a discount, it's a different order of magnitude — up to 90% cheaper, before counting the weeks you get back. Intelligence, the deepest depth, runs $300–$399 — still a fraction of what a diligence engagement costs a boutique shop, delivered same-day rather than at the end of a multi-week workstream.

The output holds up to the comparison too: a boardroom-ready PDF or editable PPTX, every insight cited to a credible source, built by a system that reasons through the data rather than summarising it. Analyst-grade insights, without the analyst retainer.
